title: Tommy McDonald Wins the 1956 Maxwell Award at Oklahoma
question: Which Oklahoma halfback won the 1956 Maxwell Award?
answer: Halfback Tommy McDonald won the 1956 Maxwell Award as the nation's top college player and finished third in that year's Heisman Trophy voting. He later reached both the College Football Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
summary: Tommy McDonald won the 1956 Maxwell Award, placed third for the Heisman, and went on to two Halls of Fame. Here is the story of the Sooner halfback.
body: Tommy McDonald did not look like a man who could take over a football game. The National Football Foundation lists the Oklahoma halfback at just 5-foot-9 and 169 pounds. Yet in 1956 he was named winner of the Maxwell Award as the best player in college football, and he finished third in the Heisman Trophy balloting.

McDonald played for the Sooners from 1954 through 1956. He earned first-team All-America honors in both 1955 and 1956, was a consensus pick as a senior, and made the all-conference team in each of those seasons. He had a nose for the end zone, too: the NFF credits him with touchdowns in 20 of 21 games across his junior and senior years, and says he was the first Sooner to score from scrimmage in every game of a season, in 1955.

He arrived in Norman from Highland High School in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and joined Bud Wilkinson's powerhouse at the height of its run. The Pro Football Hall of Fame notes that Oklahoma never lost a game during his three varsity seasons.

The story kept going after college. The Philadelphia Eagles drafted him in the third round in 1957, and he spent the next dozen years catching passes for Philadelphia, Dallas, Los Angeles, Atlanta and Cleveland. He made six Pro Bowls and played on the Eagles team that beat the Packers 17-13 in the 1960 NFL Championship Game.
Honors followed: the College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 1985, and the Pro Football Hall of Fame did the same in 1998.
